paragraphs.source_en: In the proper order of narration, I have the honor on this occasion of introducing to you this uninvited distinguished guest, the gentleman of the rafters. But before making that introduction, I must briefly set forth my humble opinion for your consideration. The gods of antiquity were revered as omniscient and omnipotent. The Christian God in particular still wears this mask of omniscience and omnipotence even today, in the twentieth century. Yet what ordinary people take for omniscience and omnipotence may at times be interpreted as ignorance and impotence. To say so is, of course, plainly a paradoxical interpretation. But since the beginning of heaven and earth, I alone have been able to pierce through the truth of this paradox. When I think of that, a certain vanity arises in me: I do not mean to boast, but I am quite a remarkable cat. For that reason, I feel I must by all means explain here why we cats are not to be looked down upon, and drive the point into the proud brains of you humans. They say that God created all things in the universe; if so, human beings too must be God's creation. Indeed, it is said that this is written explicitly in that book called the Bible. Now, concerning human beings, there is a fact which, after several thousand years of human observation, has made people feel it deeply mysterious and wondrous while inclining them ever more to acknowledge God's omniscience and omnipotence. That is to say, though human beings swarm everywhere throughout the vast world, not one of them has the same face as another. Of course, everyone has the same facial features, and their sizes are, on the whole, much alike. In other words, they are all made from the same materials, yet although the materials are the same, the result is that not one identical person has been produced. When one thinks that so many different faces could be made from such simple materials, one cannot help deeply admiring the manufacturer's skill. Without astonishing originality, it would be impossible to produce such endlessly varied faces. Even if a master painter of an age exhausted all his thought and energy trying to depict different variations of appearance, he could manage no more than a dozen or thirteen faces; from this, one cannot help admiring that God's skill in creating human beings is indeed extraordinary. After all, this is a profound skill that cannot be found in human society, so it may quite fairly be called an omnipotent skill. On this point, human beings seem to hold God in boundless awe. Naturally, from the human point of view, this reverence is entirely reasonable. But from a cat's point of view, the very same fact may instead be interpreted as proof of God's incapacity. Even if He is not wholly incapable, I think it can still be concluded that God's ability does not surpass man's. True, God made as many faces as there are people; but did He from the very beginning have a clear plan and create all these different faces by design? Or, in the course of manufacture, did He intend to make Tom, Dick, and Harry all with the same face, fail to achieve it, botch every person He made, and end up with this chaotic jumble? No one can say for certain which it is.

units.source_en: In the proper order of narration, I have the honor on this occasion of introducing to you this uninvited distinguished guest, the gentleman of the rafters.
units.source_zh: 作为叙述的正常顺序，我有幸趁此机会把这位不请自来的贵客——梁上君子向诸位作一番介绍。

units.source_en: But before making that introduction, I must briefly set forth my humble opinion for your consideration.
units.source_zh: 但在介绍之前我得聊述鄙见，以供各位参考。

units.source_en: The gods of antiquity were revered as omniscient and omnipotent.
units.source_zh: 古代的神是被尊为全智全能的。

units.source_en: The Christian God in particular still wears this mask of omniscience and omnipotence even today, in the twentieth century.
units.source_zh: 尤其是基督教的神，即便是在二十世纪的今天，仍然是一副全智全能的架势。

units.source_en: Yet what ordinary people take for omniscience and omnipotence may at times be interpreted as ignorance and impotence.
units.source_zh: 但是俗人所感到的全智全能，有时也可解释为无智无能。

units.source_en: To say so is, of course, plainly a paradoxical interpretation.

ja.t: かにパラドックスである。

units.source_zh: 这样说，显然是似是而非的解释。

units.source_en: But since the beginning of heaven and earth, I alone have been able to pierce through the truth of this paradox.

ja.t: しかるにこのパラドックスを

units.source_zh: 但是能道破这种似是而非的道理的，开天辟地以来却只有我一个。

units.source_en: When I think of that, a certain vanity arises in me: I do not mean to boast, but I am quite a remarkable cat.
units.source_zh: 一想到这点，我便产生出一种虚荣心：不是在下自吹自擂，我也是个满了不起的猫儿嘛。

units.source_en: For that reason, I feel I must by all means explain here why we cats are not to be looked down upon, and drive the point into the proud brains of you humans.
units.source_zh: 为此，我想无论如何也得在这里讲一讲不要小看我们猫儿的理由，以便把它塞进高傲的各位人的头脑里。

units.source_en: They say that God created all things in the universe; if so, human beings too must be God's creation.
units.source_zh: 据说宇宙万物都是神创造的，这样说来人也是神创造的喽。

units.source_en: Indeed, it is said that this is written explicitly in that book called the Bible.
units.source_zh: 据说在《圣经》上就是这样明确记述的。

units.source_en: Now, concerning human beings, there is a fact which, after several thousand years of human observation, has made people feel it deeply mysterious and wondrous while inclining them ever more to acknowledge God's omniscience and omnipotence.
units.source_zh: 那么，关于人的问题，事实上人本身和数千年的观察，一方面感到十分玄妙不可思议，一方面又更加倾向于承认神的全智全能。

units.source_en: That is to say, though human beings swarm everywhere throughout the vast world, not one of them has the same face as another.

ja.t: もかようにうじゃうじゃいるが

units.source_zh: 这就是说，虽然在大千世界中到处都是蠢动着的人，然而却没有一个面孔是相同的。

units.source_en: Of course, everyone has the same facial features, and their sizes are, on the whole, much alike.
units.source_zh: 当然面孔上谁都具有五官，它们的大小也是大体相差无几。

units.source_en: In other words, they are all made from the same materials, yet although the materials are the same, the result is that not one identical person has been produced.
units.source_zh: 换句话说，他们都是由同一种材料制造出来的，尽管材料相同，但结果却没有创造出一个相同的人。

units.source_en: When one thinks that so many different faces could be made from such simple materials, one cannot help deeply admiring the manufacturer's skill.
units.source_zh: 一想到用这样简单的材料居然能造出这么多不同的面孔，就不能不使人深深佩服那制造者的本领。

units.source_en: Without astonishing originality, it would be impossible to produce such endlessly varied faces.
units.source_zh: 如果没有惊人的独创力是不可能制造出这种千变万化的面孔来的。

units.source_en: Even if a master painter of an age exhausted all his thought and energy trying to depict different variations of appearance, he could manage no more than a dozen or thirteen faces; from this, one cannot help admiring that God's skill in creating human beings is indeed extraordinary.
units.source_zh: 即使一代的画工殚思竭虑，力求画出容貌的不同变化，也只不过能画出十二三种面孔而已，由此看来不能不使人佩服上帝创造人的伎俩，的确是超群出众的。

units.source_en: After all, this is a profound skill that cannot be found in human society, so it may quite fairly be called an omnipotent skill.
units.source_zh: 这毕竟是在人的社会中无法找得到的一种深奥的伎俩，因此满可以说它是一种全能的伎俩而当之无愧。

units.source_en: On this point, human beings seem to hold God in boundless awe.
units.source_zh: 人在这点上似乎对神怀有无限崇敬。

units.source_en: Naturally, from the human point of view, this reverence is entirely reasonable.
units.source_zh: 当然，从人的角度来说，这种崇敬是完全有它的道理的。

units.source_en: But from a cat's point of view, the very same fact may instead be interpreted as proof of God's incapacity.
units.source_zh: 但是从猫儿的角度来说，同是这一事实却也可以解释为这正好证明神的无能。

units.source_en: Even if He is not wholly incapable, I think it can still be concluded that God's ability does not surpass man's.
units.source_zh: 即便不是整个无能吧，我想仍然可以断定神的能力并未能超过人。

units.source_en: True, God made as many faces as there are people; but did He from the very beginning have a clear plan and create all these different faces by design?
units.source_zh: 不错，神是有多少人就制造了多少张面孔，但是，这是从一开始神就胸有成竹地创造出这些不同面孔呢？

units.source_en: Or, in the course of manufacture, did He intend to make Tom, Dick, and Harry all with the same face, fail to achieve it, botch every person He made, and end up with this chaotic jumble?
units.source_zh: 还是在制造过程中本想把张三李四都造成同一面孔，未能如愿以偿，每制造一个人都造得失败，结果搞成这种乱七八糟的呢？

units.source_en: No one can say for certain which it is.
units.source_zh: 这点是谁也说不清楚的。

paragraphs.source_zh: 作为叙述的正常顺序，我有幸趁此机会把这位不请自来的贵客——梁上君子向诸位作一番介绍。但在介绍之前我得聊述鄙见，以供各位参考。古代的神是被尊为全智全能的。尤其是基督教的神，即便是在二十世纪的今天，仍然是一副全智全能的架势。但是俗人所感到的全智全能，有时也可解释为无智无能。这样说，显然是似是而非的解释。但是能道破这种似是而非的道理的，开天辟地以来却只有我一个。一想到这点，我便产生出一种虚荣心：不是在下自吹自擂，我也是个满了不起的猫儿嘛。为此，我想无论如何也得在这里讲一讲不要小看我们猫儿的理由，以便把它塞进高傲的各位人的头脑里。据说宇宙万物都是神创造的，这样说来人也是神创造的喽。据说在《圣经》上就是这样明确记述的。那么，关于人的问题，事实上人本身和数千年的观察，一方面感到十分玄妙不可思议，一方面又更加倾向于承认神的全智全能。这就是说，虽然在大千世界中到处都是蠢动着的人，然而却没有一个面孔是相同的。当然面孔上谁都具有五官，它们的大小也是大体相差无几。换句话说，他们都是由同一种材料制造出来的，尽管材料相同，但结果却没有创造出一个相同的人。一想到用这样简单的材料居然能造出这么多不同的面孔，就不能不使人深深佩服那制造者的本领。如果没有惊人的独创力是不可能制造出这种千变万化的面孔来的。即使一代的画工殚思竭虑，力求画出容貌的不同变化，也只不过能画出十二三种面孔而已，由此看来不能不使人佩服上帝创造人的伎俩，的确是超群出众的。这毕竟是在人的社会中无法找得到的一种深奥的伎俩，因此满可以说它是一种全能的伎俩而当之无愧。人在这点上似乎对神怀有无限崇敬。当然，从人的角度来说，这种崇敬是完全有它的道理的。但是从猫儿的角度来说，同是这一事实却也可以解释为这正好证明神的无能。即便不是整个无能吧，我想仍然可以断定神的能力并未能超过人。不错，神是有多少人就制造了多少张面孔，但是，这是从一开始神就胸有成竹地创造出这些不同面孔呢？还是在制造过程中本想把张三李四都造成同一面孔，未能如愿以偿，每制造一个人都造得失败，结果搞成这种乱七八糟的呢？这点是谁也说不清楚的。
